newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Ex-president gets bail, expected to be freed soon.
newsitem.headline: Ex-president gets bail, expected to be freed soon.

text.p: Bangladesh's former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad on Wednesday was granted bail in the last of a series of corruption charges and was expected to be freed soon, court officials said.
They said an appellate bench of the Supreme Court granted Ershad bail in a case involving corruption charges over the purchase of defence radar.
Ershad, who seized power in a bloodless coup in 1982 and was deposed in an opposition-led people's uprising in 1990, at one time faced as many as 19 corruption charges.
The officials said Ershad could be freed later on Wednesday or Thursday. Ershad has been living in a sub-jail set up near the parliament house since winning a parliamentary seat in June elections.
Ershad was sentenced to 23 years of imprisonment in four cases for keeping illegal firearms and corruption.
The High Court last year quashed his 10-year sentence for the arms offence, and Ershad has appealed against his other convictions.
